last.summary: Added Bzip2.Oracle.Compress.Blocks (oracle/Bzip2/Oracle/Compress/Blocks.lean): `split level input (oneShot := false) : Array Block` with Block = {data (post-RLE1 bytes), crc (finalised block CRC), inUse}, following ADD_CHAR_TO_BLOCK/add_pair_to_block/flush_RL/copy_input_until_stop (bzlib.c). Blocks close when nblock >= 100000*level-19 is seen before reading the next byte; the pending run (and its CRC contribution) goes to the next block; runs cut at 255; the count byte is marked in inUse; empty input gives no blocks. Found from the C that block boundaries differ in one case depending on the driver: when the last input byte leaves nblock >= nblockMAX, bzip2 (BZ_RUN chunks + empty BZ_FINISH) puts the pending run in an extra block, while BZ2_bzBuffToBuffCompress (one BZ_FINISH) flushes it into the full block; `oneShot` selects (default = bzip2 program). Tests: tests/Bzip2/Test/CompressBlocks.lean (hand-computed RLE1/255-cut/empty/CRC guards + 28 `include_str` vectors in tests/vectors/compress-blocks/*.txt, level 1 and 9, around the limit, long runs across the boundary, both drivers), dumped from an out-of-tree libbz2 build with a debug print in BZ2_compressBlock (generate.py there reproduces them). Checked: `sh projects/bzip2/tools/verify.sh` ends with 'verify: packages: ok / sources: ok / build: ok / style: ok / axioms: ok / lint: ok / test: ok / verify: ok'; git status clean, `git diff --stat origin/master...HEAD` lists only Blocks.lean, Test/CompressBlocks.lean and tests/vectors/compress-blocks/* (31 files); all bzlib.c/compress.c line citations re-read against the source.
